precepts.text: Rahab let them down through the window and sent them to the mountain for three days: not only help, but an exit plan.
precepts.point: She let them down by a cord and told them to hide in the mountain three days: she gave them an exit. Is that you, ready to do that for your nation rather than spare this body that gets headaches and diarrhoea?
precepts.why:
When the king of Jericho sent for the men, Rahab hid them “with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof”, and sent the pursuers the wrong way. Then she went further: “Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.” “And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.”

She not only helped the prophets, she helped them with an exit. She gave them a way out and a plan: where to go, how long to hide, and when it would be safe to go their way.

These examples are in here for our learning. In these last days some brothers and sisters are going to be looked to to hide the prophets. As we build this spiritual underground railroad, some of y'all will be required to help one another, and sometimes when you help brothers and sisters you are going to put yourself in danger.

Is that you, sister? Is that you, brother? Are you ready to do that for your nation? Or are you going to sell out to keep this body that gets a headache, gets diarrhea, gets belly aches, coughing and all kind of infirmities? The scriptures tell you we have to be ready in these last days.

That is why Hebrews 13 follows it: “Let brotherly love continue.” “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Start small, in your household. Make that guest room ready to receive a guest; if you can't afford an extra room, instead of buying that leather couch, get a pullout couch. If a prophet is on the run and you can provide shelter for two days, a meal and shelter for a prophet, that is a blessing for you. That is the mindset of Rahab, and the mindset we have to have in these last days.

precepts.text: Like the woman who answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table, and Christ said, great is thy faith; Rahab is a heathen whose faith the Lord honoured.
precepts.point: Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.
precepts.why:
Rahab is a heathen, yet she says, “I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us”. That is faith and belief: a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land. She is like the woman who answered Christ, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” “Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.”

That woman knew her place and still believed, and Christ honoured it. Rahab knew the Lord had given Israel the land, believed it, and put her life on the line for it, and the Lord honoured her faith the same way.

precepts.text: The destruction of Sihon and Og on the other side Jordan was the report that reached Jericho.
precepts.point: Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.
precepts.why:
Rahab's faith came by report: “we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.” This is what she heard. “And the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon. So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.”

The destruction of Sihon and Og on the other side Jordan, none left alive, was the report that reached Jericho. When Rahab heard it, she knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people.

precepts.text: This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of thee; Rahab's melted heart is that word fulfilled.
precepts.point: Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.
precepts.why:
“This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.” The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations, and Rahab is that word fulfilled: “as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you”.

They heard the report, and they trembled. All the inhabitants of the land fainted because of Israel, exactly as the Lord said they would.

precepts.text: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace; her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her.
precepts.point: Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them.
precepts.why:
“By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.” Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line.

She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them. Her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her: she received the spies with peace and did not perish with the rest of Jericho that believed not.

precepts.text: Your terror is fallen upon us; as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt. The same nations whose hearts melted are now strengthened against disobedient Israel.
precepts.point: Eglon gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek, smites Israel, and possesses the city of palm trees, and the children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Wait a minute: it says “the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel.” Compare that with Joshua. Rahab told the spies, “I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.”

The nations had heard what the Most High did for us: “how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.” And the effect was, “as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.”

The same nations whose hearts melted are now strengthened against Israel, and the Most High is the one strengthening them, “because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.” When we kept his commandments the heathen fainted before us; when we broke them, he made Eglon strong enough to smite Israel and hold us eighteen years.

points: I want to digress for a minute, because there are a lot of you heathen that are watching us, or Gentiles that are watching us, and this comes up a lot when we say that the Bible is exclusive for the Israelites. They always bring up Rahab the harlot. So next time you all are in the street teaching and people bring up, what about Rahab — because in the New Testament they mention her faith, but they never say why they mention her faith.

And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there. Because they were going to take the land.

And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country. So somebody saw those two men and said, there are these guys that came here, they are foreigners and they were searching out our land.

And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country. So the king said, I want those men, bring them to me.

And the woman took the two men, and hid them. What did she do? And hid them. It is going to tell you why she hid them. Because in the New Testament it speaks about her faith. But listen to why she hid them.
And said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were. She said, look, these men came, and I did not tell them who you were or where you were at.

And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them. So they are looking for these men, and she misled them. She lied.
But she had brought them up to the roof of the house. She took them to the roof of the house and hid them, and lied to her own people concerning who these men were. Always put emphasis on that.

And hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof. And the men pursued after them the way to Jordan unto the fords. So they are running to go find these men, and Rahab hid them up in her house.

And as soon as they which pursued after them were gone out, they shut the gate. And before they were laid down, she came up unto them upon the roof; and she said unto the men, I know that the Lord hath given you the land. I know that your God is going to allow you to take this land. Look why she says that.
And that your terror is fallen upon us. Everybody is afraid of you, Israelites. And that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is the reason why Rahab hid them.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you. We heard what your God did to the Egyptians, who were a great and powerful kingdom. When ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed. We saw your God destroy kings, dry up the Red Sea, kill the firstborn of the Egyptians. We know that you have got a real God.

So this is the importance of people understanding how our God is, and understanding the power of God. Because the people today do not believe what God has to say that is written in prophecy. Whatever God did back then, this woman was terrified. And all she did was say, look, I do not want what you all are about to do to the city to happen to me. Because people like to bring her up to say that there is salvation for her nation. All of them got wiped out. The Lord spared them because they helped the Israelites out.

And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you. They were terrified of the Israelites. So when she found out that these two men were Israelites, she said, I am going to hide them. Because I already know how their God gets down. Remember, keep this in place for what it says in the New Testament about Rahab and her faith.
For the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath. You have got a real God backing you.

So that is for you heathen that are watching, you Gentiles that are watching, that are thinking that God's hand is not going to go according to plan. Because you all keep asking, what can we do? Do like Rahab did. Do like Rahab did and hold us down, so you can spare your town.

Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness. Since I did not let my people get you. That ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house. Do not kill me and my family. That is all this is about. Because based on what she saw concerning the God of Israel, she believed, this could happen to me. He destroyed the Egyptians. He destroyed the Amorites. He destroyed these other nations. And I know you all came here, you all mean business. Make a deal with me. I will not tell the people where you are, if you do not kill me and my parents.

And give me a true token: and that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death. Do not kill us. That was the faith of Rahab: that if I go on the mercy of these Israelite men, they will spare me. Because you people, now, who God is for, you will not ask the Lord for mercy to spare you from what is going on here. But a heathen, a Gentile, when they saw the works of the Lord and they knew — look, whatever I have got to do, because your God is so great, is so marvellous, if it means getting all my people killed to spare my life and my house, could we work a deal out, please?

And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. And it shall be, when the Lord hath given us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with thee. We will not wipe your whole family out.

Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall. And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.

And the men said unto her, We will be blameless of this thine oath which thou hast made us swear. He said, we want to be blameless of this oath that you made us swear. Meaning, if anything goes wrong, we do not want you to blame us. So this was the deal that they made.

Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by. Because we are going to tear everything up, so your house does not get touched. Put this red cloth in the window so I can let the army know, leave that house alone, she is the girl that hooked us up.

And thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee. Bring all your family members into your house, because that is the only way they are going to protect it. But she was letting them know, we are about to lay this whole place down. Every house is going to get touched.

And it shall be, that whosoever shall go out of the doors of thy house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head. Do not let none of your family members step outside. Their blood is going to get spilled.

And we will be guiltless: and whosoever shall be with thee in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand be upon him. And if thou utter this our business, then we will be quit of thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.

And she said, According unto your words, so be it. And she sent them away, and they departed: and she bound the scarlet line in the window. And they went, and came unto the mountain, and abode there three days, until the pursuers were returned: and the pursuers sought them throughout all the way, but found them not.

So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain, and passed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and told him all things that befell them: and they said unto Joshua, Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land. This is going to be easy, to kill everybody. For even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. That woman told them the reason why you are going to win is because everybody is afraid. And then she kept it a secret. She said, I am not going to tell them.

The king of Jericho sent to Rahab for the men, and she hid them under the flax on the roof and sent the pursuers the wrong way: some brothers and sisters will be looked to to hide the prophets, and helping will put you in danger.
Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there.

Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth. She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there.

She told the king's men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest: men came unto me, but I wist not whence they were, and they went out about the time of the shutting of the gate; pursue after them quickly. The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance to escape. A heathen woman looked out for Israel, and she did it out of the fear of the Lord, as her own words show.

Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.

Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.

Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them.

Rahab asked the spies to swear unto her by the Lord, since she had shewed them kindness, that they would shew kindness unto her father's house and give her a true token, saving her father, mother, brethren, and sisters alive.

The men answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business: since she looked out for Israel, Israel would look out for her, on condition the plan stayed secret. If she uttered the business, the oath was null and void.
She sent them to the mountain to hide three days until the pursuers returned, said according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window.

The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was upon the town wall. That scarlet line marked her house so no one in it would be slain when Israel came into the land; the terms were that whosoever went out of the doors into the street, his blood would be on his own head, and whosoever stayed within, his blood on Israel's head if any hand touched him.
The spies abode in the mountain three days until the pursuers returned, having sought them throughout all the way and found them not.

They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised.
